title.value: A Kernel Perspective on Behavioural Metrics for Markov Decision Processes
title.justification: The paper explores the application of kernel methods to define behavioural metrics in reinforcement learning, focusing on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs).
title.quote: A Kernel Perspective on Behavioural Metrics for Markov Decision Processes

extractions.description: The paper introduces a kernel-based approach to behavioural metrics in reinforcement learning, specifically in Markov Decision Processes. It provides a novel metric that is equivalent to the MICo distance, demonstrates theoretical properties, and shows practical applications in reinforcement learning.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on the mathematical and algorithmic development of reinforcement learning metrics, without a direct emphasis on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Behavioural metrics have been shown to be an effective mechanism for constructing representations in reinforcement learning. We present a novel perspective on behavioural metrics for Markov decision processes via the use of positive definite kernels.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on theoretical developments in machine learning for reinforcement learning, which does not have a direct linkage to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
primary_category.quote: We introduce the concept of a positive-definite kernel on Markov decision processes as a measure of behavioural similarity between states. This new perspective is valuable in itself, as it enables us to leverage reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) theory for a better understanding of state metrics.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper is highly specialized in machine learning concepts and does not address secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
secondary_categories.quote: We leverage this new perspective to define a new metric that is provably equivalent to the recently introduced MICo distance (Castro et al., 2021).

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any sub-category under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development as it focuses on reinforcement learning and kernel methods, which are technical areas unrelated to the given sustainable development categories.
primary_sub_category.quote: These are two crucial properties when using behavioural metrics for reinforcement learning representations.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: A general value function approximator can be seen as a composition of a m-dimensional embedding φ : X → Rm, which maps a state space X to a m-dimensional space Rm.

applications.justification: The paper discusses the application of behavioural metrics for reinforcement learning, highlighting their theoretical and empirical effectiveness.
applications.quote: We complement our theory with strong empirical results that demonstrate the effectiveness of these methods in practice.
